sentences.text: 2. The applicants are one and the same in all these bail applications.

They are accused Nos. 6 and 7,
3 and 4, 5 and 6, 6 and 7 and 7 and 8 respectively in the following crimes - B.A.No.1469/2026 pertains to Crime No.626/2025, B.A.No.1472/2026 pertains to Crime No.659/2025,
B.A.No.1475/2026 pertains to Crime No.637/2025, B.A.No.1482/2026 pertains to Crime No.638/2025 and B.A.No.1484/2026 pertains to Crime No.639/2025 of Elamakkara Police Station,
Ernakulam District.
3. The offences alleged are punishable under Sections 316(2) and 318(4) read with Section 3(5) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 and Sections 406 and 420 read with Section 34 of the IPC.

4. The prosecution case, in short, is that the B.A.No.1469/2026 and Con.Cases 2026:KER:29682 applicants along with the remaining accused with intention to deceive the respective defacto complainants, made them to believe that their company will provide 12.5% to 14.87% annual interest for the investment and obtained deposits from them through account transactions and thereafter cheated them without giving the interest as agreed or repaying the principal amount.
5. I have heard the learned counsel for the applicants and the learned Senior Public Prosecutors.
Perused the case diary.
6. The learned counsel for the applicants submitted that the applicants are innocent and have been falsely implicated in the present case.
The counsel further submitted that no materials are on record to connect the applicants with the alleged crime; hence, they are entitled to bail.

The learned Senior Public Prosecutors, on the other hand, submitted that the alleged incident occurred as part of the applicants' intentional criminal acts, and if they are released on bail at this stage, it will affect the course of the investigation.
7.
The law regarding the grant or refusal of pre- arrest bail is well settled.
Pre-arrest bail cannot be granted as a matter of course.
The power under Section 482 of BNSS could be exercised only when a special case is made out, that too, recording B.A.No.1469/2026 and Con.Cases 2026:KER:29682 reasons thereof.

Perusal of the case diary reveals that the accusation made against the applicants is very serious in nature, and it prima facie shows a premeditated criminal act on their part.
8.
The accused No.1 is the Managing Director, the accused No.2 is the Director and the applicant No.1 is the employee of Melkar Finance and Leasing Private Limited.
The applicant No.2 is the wife of the applicant No.1.
The accused No.1 was arrested in a connected crime (Cr.No.491/2025 of Thrissur Town East Police Station) on 15.10.2025.
On that day itself, a sum of 1,50,00,000/- was transferred to the account of the applicants.

In the confession statement given by the accused No.1,
it is stated that the said amount was paid to the applicants to pay back the amount due to the depositors.
The learned counsel for the applicants submitted that those amounts were paid towards the loan availed by the applicants from the company.

I had directed the learned counsel for the Manoj Paul vs State Of Kerala on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141910876/
6 applicants to produce the document, if any, to show that the said amount was towards the loan transaction.

entities.text: Manoj Paul vs State Of Kerala
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: But no such document was produced.
So there is absolutely no explanation for the receipt of 1,50,00,000/- by the applicants.
The investigation is in a preliminary stage.
The custodial interrogation of the applicants is necessary for the investigation.
B.A.No.1469/2026 and Con.Cases 2026:KER:29682

As rightly argued by the learned Senior Public Prosecutors, the possibility of the applicants influencing the witnesses and interfering with the investigation cannot be ruled out if they are released on bail.

Considering the gravity of the offence and stage of the investigation, I am of the view that these are not a fit cases where the extraordinary jurisdiction vested with this Court under Section 482 of BNSS could be invoked.
The bail applications are, accordingly, dismissed.

Sd/-
